messages:
maria: kicking off a dark-launch run to compare scheduler window vs max_batch_tokens tradeoffs across region/hardware. goal: measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and tenant fairness for cont-batcher under mixed small/large seqs.

sahil: SGTM. which model + quantization are we using for this? mosaicml-14b-q4? or try 13b first?

maria: start with mosaic13b-q4 on H100 and A100 to keep compute comparable. we should also run float16 baseline on A100 for kernel sensitivity.

jonah: added a tiny YAML for the experiment. use tilt_weight=0.25, window_ms=[4,8,16,32], max_batch_tokens=[512,1024,2048], tenant_mix=70/30 small/large. run for 30m per cell.

carla: pls post the run command. I'll kick off in ap-northeast-1 and us-west-2

maria: command I used:
```bash
run_experiment \n  --model mosaic13b-q4 \n  --kernel auto \n  --window_ms 4,8,16,32 \n  --max_batch_tokens 512,1024,2048 \n  --tenant_mix 0.7,0.3 \n  --duration 1800 \n  --regions ap-northeast-1,us-west-2 \n  --instances h100,a100 \n  --out s3://redwood-experiments/scheduler-window-darklaunch/1771112223/
```

sahil: nice. also set kernel_pref=prefer_fused_attention in one pass to capture kernel switch effects.

maria: yep added a second sweep with kernel_pref=prefer_fused_attention. run IDs:
- 1771112223-01: kernel=auto
- 1771112223-02: kernel=prefer_fused_attention

jonah: started the jobs in us-west-2 (h100) and ap-northeast-1 (a100). Will ping when first 10m windows are uploaded.

ops-bot: Job 1771112223-01 us-west-2/h100: stage=running; containers=6

carla: quick reminder — enable per-tenant trace sampling=1% to collect tail patterns

maria: traces on.

(10m later)

jonah: first metrics uploaded: s3://redwood-experiments/scheduler-window-darklaunch/1771112223/01/metrics.csv

maria: parsing. initial impressions: window_ms=4 lowers p50 but p95 regresses for mixed large sequences on H100. max_batch_tokens=2048 reduced throughput for small sequences.

sahil: paste quick pivot table?

maria:
window_ms | max_tokens | p50_ms | p95_ms | tok/s
4         | 512        | 38     | 280    | 1500
32        | 2048       | 72     | 320    | 2200
8         | 1024       | 44     | 200    | 1900

carla: 32ms window pushes throughput but p95 still high when large seqs interleave. maybe KV cache eviction or kernel tiling causing spikes.

jonah: pulling per-request kernel selection traces.

maria: traces show kernel fallback to generic_attention during long sequences, and microburst coalescing delaying small requests behind a large batch.

sahil: fairness hurting small tenants. tilt_weight low prioritizes throughput.

maria: with tilt_weight=0.25 small requests get deprioritized when a large request arrives and window is larger.

carla: run ablation with tenant_mix 50/50.

maria: started 50/50 ablation (run 1771112223-03).

(20m later)

maria: 50/50 ablation: p95 for small requests drops ~30% with window=32 and max_tokens=2048. fairness hit is workload-composition dependent.

jonah: suggests dynamic tilt_weight that increases when small-request fraction or tail latency rises.

sahil: also adaptive max_batch_tokens: cap effective batch tokens if >X small requests waiting.

maria: logged GH issue: github.com/redwood-inference/cont-batcher/issues/452 — draft policy dynamic-tilt + adaptive-max-tokens.

carla: kernel-level regression between h100 and a100?

maria: a100 (kernel=auto): slightly higher p50 but p95 comparable once kernel_pref=prefer_fused_attention enabled. fused kernels helped tail on A100.

sahil: kernel selection matters per hardware and interacts with window sizing. actions:
1) build dynamic-tilt prototype
2) add adaptive max_batch_tokens heuristic
3) follow-up 4h validation across regions and tenant shapes
4) generate explainer plots for p50/p95 vs window and max_tokens per region/hw

jonah: I'll generate plots from CSVs and upload.

maria: note ops-bot flagged a pod OOM in us-west-2 during max_tokens=2048 on H100 — check memory headroom when increasing max tokens.

ops-bot: Pod redwood-contbatcher-19 OOMKilled at 1771112800

carla: lowering max_tokens default to 1024 in prod until dynamic sizing is ready.

sahil: +1. add perf test to CI to run short smoke across kernels to catch regressions.

maria: opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1287

maria: summary: small window (4–8ms) better for small-request tail; larger windows (16–32ms) improve throughput but hurt small-tenant tail when workload skewed. kernel_pref helps on A100. next: implement dynamic-tilt and adaptive max_batch_tokens, run 4h validation across regions.

sahil: great. @jonah ping when plots are up :rocket:

jonah: uploading visualizations now. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
